body.p: The Non-Final Office Action dated January 16, 2024 has been carefully reviewed. Claims 1- 10 and 14-19 have been amended. Claims 1-19 are now pending in this application. Favorable consideration and allowance of this application is respectfully requested in light of the following amendments and remarks.
I. Claim Rejection - 35 U.S.C. §103

Claims 1, 3-7, 14-16, and 18-19 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over "Spacecraft Formation Flying System Design and Controls for Four Nanosats Mission" by Song et al. ("Song") in view of WIPO Publication 1993/009029 to Stuart et al. ("Stuart"). Claim 2 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of WIPO Publication 2018/037424 to Satak et al. ("Satak"). Claim 9 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and Satak and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 8,334,809 to Nichols et al. ("Nichols"). Claims 10-13 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of Nichols. Claim 8 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of U.S. Publication No. 2018/02514240 to Rettman et al. ("Rettman"). Claim 17 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of Russian Patent No. 2668378 to Viktorovich et al. ("Viktorovich").
A. Independent Claims 1 and 16

Applicant has amended independent claims 1 and 16 to clarify the differences between the present invention and the cited art and to further distinguish the present invention from the drift control system disclosed in the Song reference.

Independent claim 1 has been amended to clarify that the satellite formation of the present invention includes at least three satellites arranged in a multi-satellite formation supporting continuous beam steering operations for at least one of collecting observation data from an event in the sky and tracking a moving object whose observation data currently is collected. Claim 1 has been further amended to define that the control system is configured to dynamically and continuously change, based at least partly on observation data obtained by the combined radiation pattern from the multi-satellites formation, at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes

p.u: of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations in that the combined radiation pattern of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation thereby is dynamically and continuously changed and adapted to at least one of collecting observation data from an event in the sky and the movements and observation requirements of the object whose observation data is currently collected.

body.p: As amended, independent claim 16 defines the multi-satellite formation as forming a

combined radiation pattern involving the radiation from at least one observation antenna array of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation. Claim 16 has been further amended to define that the method is including the step of controlling, by the control system and at least partly based on observation data collected by the combined and continuously changing radiation pattern from said at least two satellites each comprising at least one observation antenna array , the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the multi-satellite formation by sending commands to the propulsion system to thereby change at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation and the combined radiation pattern from the observation antenna arrays of the at least two separate satellites for improved tracking and beam steering operations in that the combined radiation pattern of the antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation thereby is adapted to at least one of collecting observation data from an event in the sky and the movements of the object whose observation data is currently collected.

Support of the above amendments can be found at least on page 8, lines 5-18, page 9, lines 16-23, page 10, lines 10-18, page 1, lines 10-16, page 4, lines 11-17, page 7, lines 3-7, and dependent claims 2, 3, 18, and 19 of the application as filed.
Song relates to a spacecraft formation flying system design and control for a mission
involving four nanosats in a predetermined formation and moving in similar orbital planes. The nanosats in the predetermined formation may occasionally drift apart.

Song describes a satellite formation with four nanosats where the relative distance between the nanosats can be decreased and increased between along-track and cross-track formations, respectively, via orbit controls in the desired duration. The problem addressed in Song is that nanosats that move along similar orbital planes in a predetermined formation drift

apart owing to the difference in orbital drift rate. The drift recovery control is performed several times because of thrust limitations and control errors. The orbital control for the formation flying system in Song shall maintain the relative distance to prevent the nanosats from passing through each other, see for example column 1 on pages 151 and 152, and the text to Fig. 4.

On page 150, column 2 and Figs. 3 a)-b), Song describes two modes of operation where the nanosats may be arranged in either along-track formation to collect temporal data or in cross- track formation to collect spatial data.

On page 151, column 1 and Figs 4 a)-d), Song describes a sequence of four subsequent types of predetermined phases and orbit controls including a "Launch & Early Orbit Phase", an "Along-track Formation Phase", a "Cross-track Formation Phase" and a "Reconfiguration" phase in which the distance between the rightmost and leftmost satellites along the cross-track direction is increased.
Song thus proposes a few predetermined modes of operation including a first

predetermined along-track formation adapted for collecting temporal data and a (subsequent) predetermined cross-track formation adapted for collecting spatial data. Song addresses the problem that nanosats moving along similar orbital planes drift apart owing to the difference in orbital drift rate by orbital control using a thrust module that maintains the relative distance between the nanosats to prevent the nanosats from passing through each other.

The drift recovery control system disclosed in the Song reference is silent to controlling, based on observation data collected by an antenna array of at least one of satellites in a multi- satellite formation, the combined radiation pattern of a multi-satellite formation comprising the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites to thereby perform beam-steering operations.
In the along-track formation phase, the relative distance between each nanosat should

increase by several thousand kilometers. The period is expected to be one month. During the data collection phase of temporal differences, i.e. no combined radiation pattern from antenna arrays of separate satellites, the relative distances between each nanosat is reduced from thousands of kilometers to less than tens of kilometers. The nanosats are made to come closer steadily for 3 months during the along-track formation phase. In the cross-track formation, the size of the satellites in Song gradually increases to over 100 kilometers at the equator and covers a latitude
of 70 degrees over 3 months, see e.g. sections 2.3.1. and 2.3.2., left column on page 151 and page 152 of Song.

Hence, the dual-mode satellite system disclosed in Song, including an along-track mode and a cross-track mode, does not disclose a multi-satellite formation with a combined radiation pattern in the sense of the present invention and thereby does not allow for beam steering operations where, based on observation data collected by the combined radiation pattern from the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in a multi-satellite formation, the combined radiation pattern of the antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi- satellite formation is dynamically and continuously adapted to at least one of collected observation data from an event in the sky and the movements and observation requirements of the object whose observation data is currently collected.

In particular, Song does not disclose a multi-satellite formation where the control system is configured to dynamically and continuously change, based at least partly on observation data obtained by the combined radiation pattern from the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellites formation, at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi- satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations in that the combined radiation pattern of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi- satellite formation is dynamically and continuously changed and adapted to at least one of collected observation data from an event in the sky and the movements and observation requirements of the object whose observation data is currently collected.

The above deficiencies of Song cannot be cured by the remaining cited prior art. For instance, the claims, page 4 and FIG. 1 of Stuart discloses a spacecraft designs for a Satellite Communication System including a hemispherical, high-gain, electronically-steered antenna array (12) that is always pointed toward the Earth (E) and where the interior of the dome-shaped antenna array (12) is used to store solar cell panels (16) which unfurl through an opening (15) in a space-facing array (18) when the spacecraft (10) reaches its final orbit. Stuart deals with a constellation of satellites (10 satellites is stated) with the purpose of providing higher revisit times for communications purposes. This entails that the satellites are very far apart (100s of kilometers). The antenna pattern and reconfigurability of the antenna beam is for directing towards various earth communication stations that are in view of the satellite. On the contrary,

the present invention, as defined by the claims, entails a close formation multi-satellite mission that provides a "virtual aperture" formed by the steerable antennas on board each of the individual satellites in the formation, in order to carry out remote sensing and object observation. The re-adjustment and the control of the formation is triggered by the requirements of the observed object. This will not be possible and is not related by any means to a constellation of satellites. There is a distinct difference between close formation flying missions and satellite constellations, in terms of objectives but also technical needs. Stuart therefore fails to remedy at least the above-mentioned deficiencies of Song.

Referring now to Satak, on page 16 and FIG. 4 of Satak, an exemplary architecture of a space internet network is illustrated and described. The space internet network comprises a Satellite Constellation 401, a plurality of Earth Internet Gateways 402a... 402n and a plurality of User Terminals 403a, 403b, 403c... 403n. The Satellite Constellation 401 comprises a plurality of satellites 401a, 401b... 401n. The Satellite Constellation 401 forms a network in space, that enables a communication between the plurality of satellites 401a, 401b... 40 in and the plurality of Earth Internet Gateways 402a... 402n. Satak fails to remedy at least the above-mentioned deficiencies of Song.
Referring now to Nichols, claim 24 and FIG. la of Nichols discloses an antenna

including a first planar array of antenna elements and one or more side planar arrays of antenna elements, each side array adjacent to the first array and tilted at a predetermined angle relative to the first array. The antenna may also include a plurality of transmit/receive modules, each module coupled to one antenna element. Each transmit/receive module includes phase shifters for varying the relative phases of the antenna elements to form a desired overall beam pattern, and a low noise amplifier and high-power amplifier for amplifying signals received and transmitted by the antenna element, respectively. As such, Nichols fails to remedy at least the above-mentioned deficiencies of Song.

Referring now to Rettman, Paragraph [0040] of Rettman discloses a hall effect thruster and a gridded ion thruster using electrostatic actuation for changing the movement and direction of a satellite. As a result, Rettman also fails to remedy at least the above-mentioned deficiencies of Song.
Finally referring to Viktorovich, FIGS. 1-3 and 6 of Viktorovich discloses a spacecraft comprising a radiation sensor. Viktorovich fails to remedy at least the above-underlined deficiencies of Song.

As a result of the above, independent claim 1, as amended, distinguishes over Song, and Song in combination with any and all of the other references Stuart, Satak, Nichols, Rettman and Viktorovich cited in the Final Office Action, by defining a satellite system comprising a control system that is configured to control the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in a multi-satellite formation including at least three satellites at least partly based on observation data received by the control system from the combined radiation pattern of the at least one observation antenna arrays of at least two separate antennas in the multi-satellite formation.

In particular, amended claim 1 distinguishes over Song in combination with any of the other cited references by defining a control system configured to control the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the multi-satellite formation at least partly based on observation data collected by the combined radiation pattern of the at least one observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in a multi-satellite formation to thereby change the combined radiation pattern of the multi-satellite formation by changing the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of at least two observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation and thereby provide for improved beam steering operations when tracking a moving object whose observation data is currently collected in that the combined radiation pattern of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi- satellite formation thereby is dynamically and continuously changed and adapted to at least one of collected observation data from an event in the sky and the movements and observation requirements of the object whose observation data is currently collected.

Claim 16, as amended, distinguishes over Song, and Song in combination with any and all of the other references Stuart, Satak, Nichols, Rettman and Viktorovich cited in the Final Office Action, by defining a method for dynamically controlling the configuration and shape of a multi-satellite formation comprising at least three satellites that includes the step of controlling, by the control system and based on observation data collected by the combined radiation pattern from at least one observation antenna array of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation, the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on observation data collected by the combined radiation pattern from at least one of the observation

p.u: antenna arrays of the at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation and that is received by the control system.

body.p: In particular, amended claim 16 distinguishes over Song, and Song in combination with any and all of the other references cited in the Final Office Action, by defining a method including the step of controlling, by the control system, the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on observation data collected by the combined radiation pattern from at least one of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation to thereby change the relative angle directions of the combined radiation pattern and radiation lobes of at least two antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation for improved beam steering operations when at least one of collecting observation data from an event in the sky and tracking a moving object whose observation data is currently collected.

Hence, no combination of the above-mentioned references teaches each and every of the above-underlined distinguishing features and limitations found in claims 1 and 16, or any of the claims that depend therefrom.

In light of the above, Applicant contends that amended independent claims 1 and 16 are patentably distinct from the cited prior art. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection of independent claims 1 and 16 under 35 U.S.C. §103, along with all claims depending therefrom.
B. Dependent Claim 5

Regarding amended claim 5, there is no indication in Song of any pre-known knowledge that enables the use of artificial intelligence (that works based on a dataset that enables the prediction of the best possible formation configuration for the current requirements of the observed object/phenomenon. In amended claim 5, pre-known knowledge refers to previously acquired information or established data that the system can use to make informed decisions. When combined with artificial intelligence, this allows the control system to more effectively predict and adjust the propulsion needs, optimizing satellite formation and performance.

In Song, "four nanosats shall observe the temporal and spacial physical phenomena in space", which does not indicate any pre-known knowledge, as it refers to the actual data observation in which the formation is initially lined in an along-track formation in order to
observe the phenomena temporally, and then rearranged in a cross-track formation in order to observe the phenomena spatially. This discrepancy of Song cannot be cured by the remaining cited art.
In light of the above, Applicant contends that dependent claim 5 is patentably distinct
from the cited prior art. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection of dependent claim 5 under 35 U.S.C. §103.
In light of the amendments and remarks above, Applicant believes the application is in condition for allowance.
